kf1.tip: Explain to a Year 7 in 30 words or fewer how Elizabeth's humanist education and her imprisonment under Mary I each gave her a different tool for ruling.
kf1.note: Her education gave her the confidence to argue with ministers and bishops. Her imprisonment under Mary I gave her caution, so she avoided being trapped by her own decisions. A good answer keeps the two tools separate: education gave her brains and confidence, the Tower gave her care and secrecy. If you mixed them up or only named one, check the box again.

kf2.tip: Apply patronage to a school or club you know: name one reward like Elizabeth's monopolies, lands or offices, and say what happens if the rewards stop flowing.
kf2.note: A good answer names a reward the leader controls, such as a captain's armband or a prefect badge, and links it to Elizabeth's offices or monopolies. It then says that people stay loyal by competing for the reward, not by being forced. The trap is stopping there. You must say what happens when rewards stop: rivals stop competing and may unite or rebel, as Essex did after losing his sweet wine monopoly.

cs1.tip: Sketch the Rainbow and Armada Portraits from memory and label one symbol on each with the message it sent to ambassadors and nobles.
cs1.note: Your Rainbow Portrait sketch should show eyes and ears on her robe, labelled as a message that she is an all-seeing ruler. Your Armada Portrait, painted after 1588, should show her hand on a globe, labelled as a claim to English mastery of the seas. A good label says who saw it, ambassadors and nobles, and why: she had no husband or strong army, so image did that work.
